key_insight: LLMs with stronger small-world connectivity in their internal attention graphs tend to show better reasoning performance, and this structure can be used to identify important heads.
engineering_relevance: The paper suggests a practical sparsity-allocation strategy for model compression and pruning that preserves performance by targeting structurally important components.
method: Build functional graphs from attention-head activation similarities.
Measure small-world index (SWI), plus head-level core and bridge scores.
Use these scores in Small-World Allocation (SWA) to guide hierarchical sparsity and pruning.
evidence_signal: Across six LLMs and multiple checkpoints, higher SWI correlated with better fluid reasoning, and SWA reduced WikiText perplexity by up to 20% while preserving small-world structure better than competing methods.
watch_item: These structural signals are correlational and may depend on how attention graphs are constructed, so transferability across architectures and tasks should be validated.
paper_title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
